(MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.
